# origincloud_network_security_group_rule (Resource)

A security group rule: the traffic it allows in one direction, to or from one peer. Set exactly one of `cidr_block`, `peer_security_group` and `same_group`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `direction` (String) Which traffic the rule applies to. One of `INGRESS`, `EGRESS`. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `project` (String) The project the security group rule is in. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `protocol` (String) The traffic the rule allows. One of `ALL`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `ICMP`. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `region` (String) The region the security group rule is in. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `security_group` (String) The security group the security group rule is in. Changing it replaces the security group rule.

### Optional

- `cidr_block` (String) The peer as an address range: where admitted traffic comes from, or where sent traffic goes to. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `description` (String) What the rule is for. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `first_port` (Number) The first port the rule matches, for `TCP` and `UDP`. Each set of ports has one spelling, and the rule reads back in it: `first_port` 0 and `last_port` 0 match every port, a `last_port` of 0 the single port `first_port`, and a `first_port` below `last_port` the range between them. Any other spelling of a set is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the one to use: `first_port` 22 and `last_port` 22 is `first_port` 22 and `last_port` 0, and 0 or 1 to 65535 is 0 and 0. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `last_port` (Number) The last port the rule matches, above `first_port`; 0 for the single port `first_port`, or with `first_port` 0 for every port. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `peer_security_group` (String) The peer as another security group of the same VPC: its members' addresses. The rule's own group is refused here with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: it is `same_group`. Changing it replaces the security group rule.
- `same_group` (Boolean) The peer as the rule's own group's members. Changing it replaces the security group rule.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The security group rule's resource name, the same as `name`.
- `name` (String) The rule's resource name.
